A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TARS and provide readable methods, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–E. Corresponding content can be matched reliably despite added material and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original scene-flow experiments on VOD and a proprietary radar dataset, including component ablations, detector analyses, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds ego-motion estimation errors and a fully supervised TARS experiment.

M1.justification: The core architecture and standard training procedure remain unchanged. Appendix B.3 adds a fully supervised TARS-ego adaptation using annotation-derived targets and disabling Lsc, Lss, Lrd, and Lopt, constituting a limited training-objective change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same VOD and proprietary datasets and driving environments. Ego-motion estimation was already trained within TARS-ego; reporting its errors and changing supervision do not introduce new task requirements or data populations.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding scene-flow, ablation, and efficiency comparisons. The added ego-motion and fully supervised tables reuse CMFlow and PV-RAFT already compared in v1, without introducing or revising baseline methods.

E3.justification: V2 adds relative translation and angular error metrics for the ego-motion head in Table A. Table H introduces a fully supervised training setting with annotation-derived targets and four losses disabled. Existing dataset splits, training schedules, and benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B.3 adds a supervision sensitivity experiment comparing fully supervised and cross-supervised TARS-ego. The earlier component, detector-size, class-wise, and emergency-case analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. V2 retains the existing aggregate-result reporting practice.

E6.justification: New Table A reports TARS-ego translation/angular errors of 0.059 m/0.098 degrees versus CMFlow's 0.083 m/0.140 degrees. Table H adds fully supervised TARS-ego results, including EPE 0.087 m and AccR 72.7%. These use different training conditions from the retained cross-supervised results of 0.092 m and 69.1%; existing benchmark values are unchanged.

T1.justification: Existing mathematical definitions and reasoning are retained. The added pseudocode restates the architecture, and the final VOD objective assembles previously described losses with a newly disclosed weight. No new theoretical result, proof, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the traffic-level rigidity contribution, detector-feature integration, tangential-motion claim, and headline improvements of 23% and 15%. Wording changes do not alter their scientific scope.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the new fully supervised experiment as evidence that TARS can benefit from more precise ground truth. Existing explanations concerning traffic context, radar sparsity, emergency situations, detector dependence, and runtime limitations remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: New Appendix A.4 supplies pseudocode for the forward pass and TVF encoder/decoder. Appendix D.2 explicitly gives the complete VOD objective and optical-loss weight of 0.1. These clarify implementation without establishing changes to the original experiments.

R1.justification: All 42 distinct cited works are retained after matching the separate main-text and appendix bibliographies in v2. The positioning relative to LiDAR rigidity methods, radar scene flow, and joint detection remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 copyedits the main text, revises headings and captions, adds a pseudocode subsection and acknowledgements, updates affiliations, and separates appendix references. The overall narrative and section organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: V2 adds supervision-summary Table 2, result Tables A and H, and Algorithms 1–3. It also adjusts diagram labels and relocates appendix displays. Existing qualitative scenes, principal table structures, and the two-column layout are retained.

improvement.justification: The pseudocode and explicit optical-loss weight improve implementation clarity, while Tables A and H add targeted validation of ego-motion estimation and supervision dependence absent from v1. These are useful incremental gains; the principal benchmark evidence and core claims remain unchanged.
